transcript: I have a big presentation on Thursday and I keep replaying every time I've messed one up before. My hands shake and I lose my train of thought. Last time I actually did fine once I got past the first two minutes, but I don't remember that part, I only remember being scared.

qa.question: What happened once you got past those first two minutes last time?
qa.answer: Honestly it went smoothly, people asked good questions and nobody seemed to notice I was nervous.

transcript: My sister keeps bringing up old stuff from years ago every time we talk, and I end up defending myself instead of just having a normal conversation. It's exhausting. We used to be really close before this started.

qa.question: What was it like when you two were close?
qa.answer: We'd talk on the phone for hours about nothing in particular. It was easy back then.

transcript: I have three deadlines colliding this week and I don't know how I'm going to get it all done. I keep starting one thing and switching to another because I panic about the others.

qa.question: Is there anything from this week that's already handled or going okay?
qa.answer: I did finish the client report yesterday ahead of schedule, so that's one less thing.

transcript: I've been wondering if my partner and I actually want the same things anymore. We don't fight, we just feel distant. I don't know if that's normal or a sign something's wrong.

qa.question: When did you last feel really connected to each other?
qa.answer: A couple weekends ago we cooked dinner together and just talked for hours, it felt easy.

transcript: I got promoted last month and instead of being excited I mostly feel like I'm going to be found out as not actually qualified. Everyone else in these meetings seems so sure of themselves.

qa.question: Has anyone given you feedback since the promotion?
qa.answer: My manager said my first project proposal was one of the clearest she's seen from someone new to the role.

transcript: I keep putting off this project and then feeling terrible about myself for putting it off, which makes it even harder to start. It's a loop I can't seem to break.

qa.question: Is there a version of starting that's felt easier before?
qa.answer: When I just open the file and do five minutes with no pressure to finish, I usually keep going longer than planned.

transcript: I've been working late every night for weeks and I don't feel like myself anymore. Things I used to enjoy just feel like one more obligation now.

qa.question: Was there a point recently where something felt less like an obligation?
qa.answer: Actually this past Sunday I went for a walk with no phone and it was the first time in weeks I felt calm.

transcript: I've been offered a new job and I keep going back and forth on whether to take it. Every time I lean one way I immediately think of a reason to lean the other way.

qa.question: What draws you toward taking it?
qa.answer: The team seemed genuinely excited to work with me, and that's rare in interviews I've had.

transcript: I went to a work social last night and spent most of it feeling like I said the wrong things. I replayed the conversations the whole drive home.

qa.question: Was there any part of the night that felt fine while it was happening?
qa.answer: Early on I had a good conversation with a coworker about a show we both like, that part was easy.

transcript: I've been thinking about a friendship that faded out a couple years ago. We just drifted, nothing dramatic happened, but I miss having someone who knew me that well.

qa.question: What do you remember most about being known that well by someone?
qa.answer: She always knew when something was actually wrong versus when I was just tired, without me explaining.

transcript: Money's been tight the last few months and I check my bank account way more than I used to, usually right before bed, which doesn't help me sleep.

qa.question: Has anything helped even a little with the money stress?
qa.answer: I made a simple spreadsheet last week and just seeing the numbers laid out made it feel less scary.

transcript: My kid has been having a rough few weeks at school and I feel like I'm failing at helping, even though I don't really know what would help.

qa.question: Has there been a moment recently where things felt a little easier with them?
qa.answer: Last night we just watched a movie together and didn't talk about school at all, and it was nice.

transcript: I had a health scare a few weeks ago that turned out to be nothing serious, but I'm still kind of shaken by how scared I was in the days before the results came back.

qa.question: What helped you get through those days of waiting?
qa.answer: My roommate sat with me the night before the appointment and just kept things normal, that helped a lot.

transcript: I haven't been able to write anything I like in months. Every time I sit down I compare it to older work and delete it.

qa.question: Is there anything from the older work you're proud of that you could revisit?
qa.answer: There's one piece from last year I still think is decent, I haven't looked at it in a while though.

transcript: My roommate and I keep having the same argument about chores and neither of us wants to bring it up directly, so it just simmers.

qa.question: Has a conversation with them ever gone well, even about something small?
qa.answer: We talked through splitting the internet bill fine last year, that was straightforward.
